problems.title: The variational expression needs an upper-bound condition
claim: The paper claims \(I(X;Z)\le U(q)=\mathbb E_{XZ}\log q(Z|X)-\mathbb E_X\mathbb E_Z\log q(Z|X)\) for a normalized neural conditional without a fitting condition.
analysis: Let independent bits \(A\) be fair and \(N\) have probability \(1/4\) of one; set \(X=(A,N)\), deterministic feature \(Z=A\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}N\). Then \(I(X;Z)=H(Z)=\log2\), while valid zero-logit conditional \(q(z|x)=1/2\) gives \(U=0\). With \(P=P_{XZ},Q=P_XP_Z,R=P_Xq\), direct cancellation yields \[U(q)-I(X;Z)=D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q\|R)-D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|R).\] Thus the missing condition is the corresponding nonnegative KL difference. A full-support binary joint with masses \((3/8,1/8;1/8,3/8)\) also has positive MI and zero surrogate under constant conditional, so zero joint probabilities are not essential.
result: The unconditional bound and resulting guaranteed bottleneck relation are invalid. Empirical architecture ranking can still be useful. This caveat is already explicit in original CLUB, Theorem 3.2.
repair: State the inequality only when \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|R)\le D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q\|R)\), with required finiteness. Fitting the conditional can help but does not by itself guarantee this condition or tightness.
problems.existing_correction_status: The original CLUB literature already states the needed condition; no author correction to this paper’s unqualified equation is established.
problems.impact_rationale: An exact deterministic-feature example contradicts the statistical guarantee central to the proposed proxy.

problems.title: Maximizing the bound is not conditional fitting
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, paragraph after Eq.(8); Algorithm 2, p.13, lines 13–15
claim: The conditional estimator parameters ascend the positive-minus-negative log-conditional expression, described as fitting/tightening the bound.
analysis: On the same deterministic distribution, choose \(q_a(Z=A|X)=\sigma(a)\), ignoring \(N\). Joint matching probability is \(3/4\), product matching probability \(1/2\), so \(U(a)=a/4\), with derivative \(1/4\) and no finite maximizer. Actual conditional likelihood is \(L(a)=3\log\sigma(a)/4+\log(1-\sigma(a))/4\), uniquely maximized at \(a=\log3\); it tends to \(-\infty\) as the printed objective increases unboundedly. In the full-support noisy binary control, the same family is well specified and the same failure holds, so misspecification is not the explanation.
result: The printed ascent cannot be interpreted as conditional maximum likelihood or general tightening. The official supplement provides final-model evaluation, not the search/estimator implementation, so historical execution attribution remains unknown.
repair: For fixed encoder/distribution, maximize joint conditional log likelihood \(\mathbb E_P\log q_\phi\), equivalent to minimizing \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|P_Xq_\phi)\), then evaluate the surrogate separately. This restores fitting, not unconditional bound validity or architecture-ranking consistency.
problems.existing_correction_status: Original CLUB Eq.(16) and Algorithm 1 use conditional likelihood fitting; adoption of that procedure in this paper’s unavailable search code is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The central estimator-training objective has an exact unbounded direction that worsens its claimed fitting goal arbitrarily.

problems.title: The stage rule reverses loss improvement and misses plateaus
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, p.7; Algorithm 3, p.14, lines 36 and 40–42
claim: Stage II stores raw loss but transitions when its mean forward difference is below \(\epsilon\operatorname{std}(W)\), using a strict comparison.
analysis: A full \(20\)-point window \((1,0.99,\ldots,0.81)\) has forward difference \(-0.01\) and positive threshold approximately \(2.3065\times10^{-6}\) at \(\epsilon=4\times10^{-5}\); the literal rule transitions during steady improvement. A constant window has both quantities zero, so strict \(0<0\) fails and no transition occurs. Restoring only a nonnegative guard does not fix raw-loss sign. Higher variance also raises the threshold, easing the comparison when improvement is held fixed.
result: The literal pseudocode conflicts with its saturation description. A hidden sign/guard correction may make the actual implementation different; no segmentation failure is asserted.
repair: Use benefit-oriented values, including negative loss, and a complete stage-specific window. A rule \(0\le\Delta\le\epsilon_{\rm abs}+\epsilon_{\rm rel}\operatorname{std}(W)\), \(\epsilon_{\rm abs}>0\), handles the displayed controls. Reset histories and define deterioration/final-stage policies; no general optimization theorem follows.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a demonstrated algorithm-specification discrepancy with unavailable runtime attribution, separate from the core MI proofs.
